chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, other than that he did not copulate with her, then he married her daughter. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he did not copulate with the mother, there is no problem, but if he did copulate with her, he cannot marry her daughter.'

key_terms.أَفْضَى إِلَى: To copulate with / to have sexual intercourse with
key_terms.الْأُمِّ: The mother (in the context of the daughter)
key_terms.بَاشَرَ: To have sexual intercourse or engage in intimate relations
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his wife's mother if he had sexual relations with the mother?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of *al-gharar* (uncertainty regarding lineage and affinity) applies specifically when full sexual intercourse (*istifda*) has occurred with the mother; mere foreplay or kissing does not establish the impediment. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between partial and full consummation in determining marital prohibitions, ensuring clarity in family lineage. The principle underscores that the barrier to marrying the daughter is rooted in the complete union with the mother, reflecting the precision of Imami fiqh in personal status law.
